content.thinking:
I'm listing the key facts for the postmortem: the cached spend figures disagreed with purchases, with 90 of 240 stale after the copies fell behind at A5 and were served from A6. There were no deploys, flags, logs, or metrics to explain it. M1 discarded the stale figures, and F1 is the page serving cached entries without checking them against purchases, with a fix proposed in PR #442.

I'm now checking the causal chain for the postmortem: the stale totals trace back to cached copies that stopped keeping up with purchases from A5, and the record doesn't show what stopped the updates. Deploys and flag changes are ruled out as the cause, but I need to confirm no earlier change explains it.

I'm working out whether the deploy and flag checks actually cover the window when the cached copies began falling behind. The deploy record covers the full day before the alert, but the flag history only reaches back an hour, which leaves the earlier part of the gap unchecked.

I'm weighing whether the flag check, which only reaches back an hour, counts as ruling anything out for the postmortem. The page serving stale entries without checking them against purchases is the mechanism, but the chain still stops at why the cached copies fell behind, since no change was recorded that set it off.

I'm working out what set the incident off: the cached copies stopped keeping up around 13:08, but the record doesn't show what changed then, and the missing check on the serving path only explains why the stale figures got through.

I'm settling the root cause for the postmortem: the cached copies stopped keeping up with purchases from A5 and pages kept serving them as current, and the record doesn't show what stopped the updates. Since no change turned up to tie to the incident, I'm marking the cause as not established and noting the missing check on the serving path as a contributing factor.

I'm checking whether the root cause rests on the missing check on the serving path: that check is the reason the stale figures got through, but the cached copies stopping their updates from A5 is what set the incident off. Since no change explains that, I'll treat the missing check as a contributing factor, and the fix in PR #442 addresses it.

I'm laying out the causal chain for the postmortem: shoppers saw spend totals behind their actual purchases, because pages were serving cached copies that had stopped keeping up with the ledger from A5. The record doesn't show what stopped those updates, so the root cause stays unestablished.

I'm checking the flag history against the window: it only reaches back an hour before the alert, so it doesn't cover the stretch from 13:08 when the copies first fell behind. The deploy record covers the full day, so that part is ruled out, but the flag check is not.

I'm now deciding how to word the ruled-out checks for the postmortem: no deploy or release on the service in the day before the alert, and no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before Argus acted. That hour doesn't reach back to when the cached spend figures stopped keeping up, so I'll say so in the wording rather than presenting it as fully ruled out.

I'm now writing the contributing factors: the account page takes a cached spend figure without checking it against the purchases it already holds, a gap Code-Fix reads in the page's files, with the stale-entry check existing only offline. Had that check run, stale entries would have been recomputed from the ledger, so shoppers would have seen correct totals even with the cache behind. Whether anything watched the cached copies keeping up between A5 and A6 is still open, since the alert only fired after they were already being served.

I'm settling how to frame the detection gap for the postmortem: no alert caught the cached spend figures stopping their updates at A5, so the gap only showed up once the stale figures were already being served. Had something flagged the stopped updates then, the figures would have been caught before shoppers saw them, which I'll note as a contributing factor with a proposed alert on the updates to those cached figures.

I'm now weighing whether a missing page alert belongs as its own contributing factor: nobody was paged when the alert fired, which is a finding in its own right rather than something that changed how the incident unfolded.

I'm deciding how to phrase the detection gap as a contributing factor: no alert fired when the cached spend figures stopped updating at A5, so the gap only surfaced once the stale figures were already being served. I'm noting a proposed alert on those updates as the follow-up.

I'm adding the action items now: one to find and restore whatever stopped the cached spend figures from keeping up with purchases, since that cause is still in place, and I'll leave its answers empty. I'm also noting that the lack of readable metrics and logs for io-shop during the investigation is worth an item of its own.

I'm adding a prevention item to restore whatever keeps the cached spend figures in step with purchases, and noting that the account page's missing check is already covered by AI-2. I'm also listing an alert on those cached figures going stale, and a paging item for CachedSpendTotalsAreStale with no answers yet, plus an item to find out why io-shop's metrics and logs returned nothing during the investigation. Since io-summary-cache belongs to checkout-platform, I'll name them as its owner.

I'm drafting the lessons section now, starting with what went well: the Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures at T19, which sent those pages back to the purchase ledger. I'm keeping that separate from whatever the store reported about what it removed.

I'm drafting the went-well section now: the Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures at T19, which sent those pages back to the purchase ledger. I'm keeping that apart from what the store reported removing, and I'm also noting that the Code-Fix Agent put a fix forward as a draft pull request for a person to review.

I'm reviewing the lessons section and deciding what goes under got-lucky: no customer lost money, but the reason for that is worth separating from the nature of the fault itself.

I'm weighing whether anything in the got-lucky section holds up: the widest gap was one purchase, so the figures shoppers saw were only slightly off, but that's really about the impact and not the kind of fault itself. I'll leave got-lucky empty for now.

I'm noting the assumptions the postmortem rests on: the metrics were unreadable, so the onset and duration come from the alert's own dates, and the flag history only covers an hour. I'm also flagging that the deployed revision was never named, so I can't confirm the files Code-Fix read are what actually ran.

I'm settling the root cause in plain terms: from the point the cached spend totals stopped being updated as purchases came in, the entries fell behind the ledger and were still served as current, and the evidence doesn't show what stopped the updates. Next I'm checking the symptom wording so shoppers' account pages are described as showing totals that were behind.

I'm checking the wording of the symptom and the figures in the causal chain, making sure each date is set off in braces, and confirming the had-it-been-otherwise line for the second contributing factor is correct.

action_items.item: Find what stopped the cached spend figures in io-summary-cache from being updated with new purchases from {A5}, and get those updates running again, working with checkout-platform, which owns io-summary-cache.
Add an alert that fires when the cached spend figures stop being updated with new purchases, separate from the check that compares the figures being served.
Link the CachedSpendTotalsAreStale alert to on-call so that a person is paged when it fires.
Find out why the investigation got no metrics and no log lines back for io-shop, and fix it.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that did not match the purchases behind them.
The pages took their spend figures from cached copies that had fallen behind the purchase ledger. The ledger itself was correct and never moved, and only the cached copies were wrong.

ruled_out.what: A deploy, release or flag change on the service in the day before the alert: none was recorded.

A flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before Argus acted: none was recorded. That hour does not reach back to {A5}, when the copies stopped keeping up, so a flag change before that hour was not ruled out.

causal_chain.step: From {A5} the cached copies stopped keeping up with new purchases, and nothing was putting them right. The record does not show what stopped the updates, and no change was found that set this off.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The saved copies of shoppers' spending totals stopped being updated when new purchases came in, and the account pages likely showed those copies without checking them against the purchases; what stopped the updates is not known.

contributing_factors.factor: Code-Fix read the account page's code in src/io_shop/account_page.py. In that reading, when the cache returns an entry, the page shows that entry's figure without comparing the purchase count stored with it to the shopper's purchases, which the page already has in hand. In the files Code-Fix read, the only check that treats a count mismatch as a sign of a stale entry is an offline reconciliation check, not on the serving path.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Each stale entry would have been worked out again from the purchase ledger, so shoppers would have seen correct figures even though the cache had stopped keeping up.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No alert was seen that would catch the cached spend figures no longer being updated. The fault was found only by the check comparing cached figures with the purchases behind them, after the stale copies were already being served.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The updates stopping at {A5} could have been caught and dealt with before stale figures were served to shoppers from {A6}.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The alert itself listed which cached figures disagreed and when the copies stopped keeping up, which gave the mitigation an exact list of entries to discard.
The Mitigation Agent discarded the stale cached figures, which sent those pages back to the purchase ledger.
Argus marked the incident mitigated after the store reported what it had removed, and that matched the whole of what was wrong.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was asked to look into why the cached figures had stopped being updated.

input.root_cause: From {A5} the cached spend totals stopped being updated as new purchases were recorded, so the cached copies fell behind the purchase ledger, which stayed correct, and account pages were served those copies from {A6}. The evidence does not show what stopped the updates.
input.still_at_risk: Nothing was keeping the cached spend figures up to date, so any shopper's figure could go stale again with their next purchase and be shown on their account page.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages showed spend totals that were behind their purchases
